What went wrong for you last year?

I sat through about forty vendor pitches last year and I can tell you exactly what happens. Somebody spends thirty minutes showing me a system doing everything perfectly, and the whole time I am sitting there thinking about the two weeks in January when nothing works and my team is doing it by hand. Nobody ever talks about that part. If a supplier opens with the migration, if they tell me before I ask how long onboarding really takes with four hundred users, my whole posture changes. That is the one that gets the second meeting. And here is the thing that vendors never seem to believe: I am not looking for the best product. I have a perfectly adequate product right now. I am looking for the one that will not become my problem in February.

We lost a deal two years ago for a reason I still think about. Everything went well, the proof of concept worked, the numbers were good, and then in the last meeting somebody asked how long the deployment would take, and my colleague said eight weeks. It was not a lie. It was optimistic. And the buyer had already called two of our clients, and both of them had told him it took about four months. So the number was not the problem. The problem was that we had said something he could check, and it did not match. If you are ever unsure, give the longer number. Nobody has ever cancelled a contract because a project finished early, and I have never once regretted saying twelve when I thought it might be eight.
